headline: Penguins’ Bryan Rust leaves game with lower-body injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Pittsburgh's Bryan Rust left Monday's 5-4 loss to the Utah Mammoth with a lower-body injury. No timeline is given in the report.

The timing stings for Pittsburgh, because Rust's numbers so far this season suggest his goals were running hot. He has three goals in six games, but his own expected goals (the quality of his chances, converted into the goals they should produce) sit at 1.55, so he is 1.45 goals above that mark. His expected-goal rate of 1.02 per 60 minutes is solid, not special, and the Penguins controlled a smaller share of the chances with him on the ice at five-on-five (about 47 percent) than they did without him. In other words, Rust's absence may cost the Penguins less production than his scoring line implies. His 29 goals last season show he's a real scorer, though, and some regression was likely anyway.

The bigger concern is the team. Pittsburgh is 3-5-1 with a 49.3 percent share of expected goals overall, and its five-on-five share is a healthier 55 percent. The Penguins are 3 goals below expected, so the record may be worse than the play. Losing a forward now, though, makes a rebound harder.
